title: The Live Contact
premise: Beatrix Ravensworth, a veteran hostage negotiator whose one unresolved failure—a jumper named Elias Crane—still haunts him, is the only person who receives a garbled mid-flight call from Flight 417 before every record of the plane vanishes from radar, manifests, and memory. The caller is a woman claiming to be a hijacker with a conscience, warning that a second, unlisted aircraft will be made to look like an accident over a crowded city. As Beatrix races to verify a crime no system admits happened, he discovers the hijacker is Elias's daughter, seeking the truth about her father's death, which ties back to the aviation insurer Beatrix once worked for. To stop the attack, Beatrix must confess his own buried role in Elias's death, trade his career for the truth, and talk the daughter down while the real conspirators close in—ending with the second plane forced to land, the insurer exposed, and Beatrix walking away from the board with his first honest failure behind him.
about_author: Y. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former crisis-line volunteer who spent six years listening to strangers on the worst nights of their lives. Ashgrove writes thrillers about people who talk for a living and the silences that undo them.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Beatrix Ravensworth's POV. A quiet night shift at the negotiation unit, a packed bag under his desk, and a ritual visit to the memorial wall where Elias Crane's case file sits unsolved. When a call comes through on his personal line from a plane that shouldn't be able to reach him, he answers out of habit. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man always ready to leave.

chapters.title: Four One Seven
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The caller, a woman using the name 'Wren,' describes a bomb rigged to look like mechanical failure and gives him eleven minutes before the line dies. He escalates to his supervisor, who finds no flight 417 in any system—no manifest, no radar trace, nothing. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding a truth no one else can see.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating Beatrix and Wren. Wren, aboard the vanished aircraft, moves through a cabin of passengers who seem oddly calm, while Beatrix digs into the airline's parent company—Meridian Assurance—and finds Elias Crane's death certificate signed by a Meridian subsidiary. Emotional beat: two strangers circling the same buried secret.

chapters.title: The Crane File
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He breaks into an offsite records depot and learns Elias was a Meridian auditor who found a scheme to write off 'loss events'—engineered disasters—before he fell from a bridge. The file lists a scheduled event: tomorrow, 6:14 p.m. Emotional beat: grief curdling into guilt as Beatrix realizes he once negotiated for Meridian.

chapters.title: What Wren Wants
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reveals to the reader—and then to Beatrix—that she is Elias's daughter, raised on her father's paranoia and his hidden ledger, and that Flight 417 is Meridian's own dry run, its passengers unknowing participants. She wants Beatrix, the negotiator who failed her father, to help her stop it. Emotional beat: fury and hope colliding in a hostage-taker who doesn't want hostages.

chapters.title: Six Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Official channels brand him a crank and suspend him; Meridian's security detail begins following him. He recruits his estranged protégé, Dana Okafor, the only colleague who trusts his instincts, and they trace the 'accident' to a regional commuter flight over Harborview Stadium. Emotional beat: found family assembling under pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Board
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana works the airport while Beatrix confronts a Meridian executive who offers him his old job, his reputation, and Elias's sealed file—in exchange for walking away. Beatrix records the offer. Emotional beat: temptation as the sharpest knife; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Meridian's fixers storm Flight 417 to silence her, and she takes the cockpit to keep the plane—and the evidence—airborne, broadcasting the ledger to every newsroom. Beatrix, on the ground, becomes her negotiator in earnest, talking her through the takeover as she spirals. Emotional beat: the failure repeating, offering him a second chance.

chapters.title: Live Contact
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the commuter jet minutes from Harborview, Beatrix goes live on air with Wren's broadcast, reading Elias's ledger and the executive's recorded offer, forcing authorities to ground the second plane. Meridian's fixers breach the cockpit; Wren is wounded holding the door. Emotional beat: climax—confession as weapon, truth as the only lever that moves the world.

chapters.title: After the Line Goes Dead
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue weeks later. Wren survives in custody, her testimony dismantling Meridian; the passengers of 417 step into daylight and memory returns to them. Beatrix closes Elias's file, unpacks the go-bag, and lets Dana buy the coffee for once. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—the price of survival paid, an inheritance of truth passed on, a found family at a diner table.
